root_cause: Multiple keydown event listeners are attached to the input field each time the autocomplete list is regenerated. When the list is filtered (e.g., after typing 'l'), a new listener is added without removing the previous one. Both listeners run on ArrowDown and Enter, causing the stale listener (with an outdated currentFocus) to click the wrong item (Blueberry) while the new listener clicks the correct item (Blackberry). The stale listener's click wins, resulting in the wrong form value.
repair_strategy: Modify the navigation controller to store the active keydown listener on the config object and remove it before adding a new one. This ensures only one navigation listener exists at any time.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter) will consistently select the currently highlighted option, improving operability for keyboard users and meeting WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Minimal risk: only affects autocomplete keyboard navigation. Custom navigation functions (if provided via config.resultsList.navigation) will also be managed correctly.
verification_requirements: Run the provided journey test: after typing 'b', two ArrowDown, 'l', ArrowDown, Enter, the form value must be 'Blackberry'.
Test ESC key closes the list and does not leave stale listeners.
Verify that rapid filtering (typing multiple characters) does not cause duplicate listeners.
